fields.rank_math_title: Estonian Company for Ukrainians %currentyear%: e-Residency and CFC
fields.rank_math_description: Opening an OÜ in Estonia for Ukrainians via e-Residency: registration, 0% tax on retained profit in Estonia, CFC rules and tax obligations in Ukraine in 2026.
fields.content_blocks_0_content:
For a Ukrainian entrepreneur, an Estonian OÜ is a European company that can be managed from Ukraine: contracts with EU clients, payment services that do not work with Ukrainian entities, and corporate income tax only when profit is paid out. Ukraine is among the top five countries by number of Estonian e-residents, and its citizens can use a dedicated programme that compensates state fees. But for a resident of Ukraine, an Estonian company lives in two tax systems at once. In Estonia: 22/78 tax on profit distributions, board member remuneration, VAT. In Ukraine: a notice and an annual report on a controlled foreign company. And if your team works in Ukraine as FOPs (Ukrainian sole proprietors), the Estonian company also gets a VAT obligation on services from abroad, something almost nobody warns about.
We register OÜs for Ukrainian entrepreneurs, provide a legal address and a contact person, keep the books and prepare financial statements so that they can be attached to the CFC report in Ukraine.

fields.content_blocks_4_step_1: Send a request and describe your business. What you do, where your clients are, whether your team in Ukraine works as FOPs, where you are tax resident and whether you have e-Residency.
fields.content_blocks_4_step_2: Get a structure. We propose the structure, the tax regime in Estonia and the list of obligations in Ukraine, check your eligibility for fee compensation and quote a fixed price.
fields.content_blocks_4_step_3: Get your e-resident card and sign the contract. The card can be collected in Kyiv or Lviv; the contract is signed with a digital signature.
fields.content_blocks_4_step_4: We register the company and start the accounting. OÜ registration, legal address and contact person, onboarding with a bank or payment institution, bookkeeping from the first month.

fields.content_blocks_7_content:
FOP in Ukraine or an Estonian OÜ: what changes

An Estonian company does not automatically replace a FOP: they are different tools for different tasks.
Parameter Group 3 FOP in Ukraine Estonian OÜ
Income tax Single tax on turnover 0% on reinvested profit; 22/78 on distribution
Contract jurisdiction Ukraine EU
Payment services Limited access to a number of international providers Stripe, Paddle, Wise and other EU providers
Reporting Ukrainian FOP tax return Estonian bookkeeping and annual report + CFC report in Ukraine
Liability All personal assets Limited to the company's capital
Fits when Clients accept a Ukrainian contractor, revenue is withdrawn immediately Clients need an EU counterparty, profit is reinvested
In practice, many entrepreneurs keep their FOP and open an OÜ in parallel, for contracts with European clients and payment services.
fields.content_blocks_8_title_right: Key insight: a team in Ukraine creates VAT in Estonia
fields.content_blocks_8_text_right: The most common model: the Estonian OÜ sells to EU clients, while developers and designers in Ukraine invoice it as FOPs. Almost nobody writes about the tax consequence of this model. Services that an Estonian company receives from a supplier outside the EU are subject to Estonian VAT under the reverse charge rule. If the OÜ is VAT-registered, it charges 24% and immediately deducts it, so the net result is zero. If the OÜ is not registered, it must register as a limited VAT payer and pay 24% on these services with no right to deduct. There is no threshold. Practical conclusion: for the "clients in the EU, team in Ukraine" model, the VAT registration question is decided by calculation, not by default. Sometimes a standard registration is more advantageous because the tax on the team's services becomes neutral. We calculate both options on your figures before the first payment to contractors.
fields.content_blocks_9_title_left: When an Estonian company does not fit and when it is not enough
fields.content_blocks_9_text_left:
An honest review saves more than the registration.
  • You live in Estonia under temporary protection. You do not need e-Residency and will not be issued it: the company can be set up with an Estonian ID card. Your tax residency may already be Estonian, in which case Ukrainian CFC rules may not apply to you.
  • You live in Poland or Germany. Tax residency is determined by the country where you live, and the Estonian company falls under its CFC rules. Residency comes first, structure second.
  • All your clients are in Ukraine. An Estonian company will add reporting but no advantages: contracts with Ukrainian clients are easier through a FOP or a Ukrainian LLC.
  • You want an Estonian VAT number "for credibility". Without an economic link to Estonia, EMTA may refuse. B2B clients in the EU are invoiced under reverse charge even without an Estonian VAT number.
  • You need to take the money out immediately. The Estonian model pays off when profit stays in the company. If everything is paid out as dividends, the 22/78 tax in Estonia plus the dividend tax in Ukraine costs more than a FOP.

fields.content_blocks_11_content:
How a Ukrainian can open and run a company in Estonia: practice

e-Residency from Ukraine

The application is submitted online in the Police and Border Guard Board environment. You need a passport, a photo and a description of why you need Estonian e-services. The state fee is €150, rising to €165 from 1 January 2027. The pick-up point is chosen in the form: the Estonian Embassy in Kyiv or the mobile pick-up point in Lviv coordinated by the embassy in Kyiv. For men of conscription age during martial law, this is often the only realistic option. The card is kept at the pick-up point for 6 months. More in our article how to obtain e-Residency in 2026.

Fee compensation: conditions

Condition Requirement
Citizenship Ukraine
e-resident status Obtained on or after 24 February 2022
Provider Participates in the compensation programme
Company New, registered by 31 December 2026
Previous companies Before 24 February 2022 you did not own Estonian companies or sit on their boards
Amount Up to €150 for e-Residency and €265 for company registration
The compensation is paid only for both operations together and is not refunded if e-Residency is refused. It is paid by the provider, which is then reimbursed by the programme.

Taxes in Estonia

As long as profit stays in the company, there is no corporate income tax. On distribution, the company pays 22/78. A board member's remuneration is subject in Estonia to 22% income tax and 33% social tax, even if you live in Ukraine. More in our article Estonian corporate tax in 2026.

CFC in Ukraine

Obligation Deadline What matters
CFC notice 60 days after the event Setting up the company, change of shareholding, start of actual control
CFC report Every year, together with the income tax return Filed even with zero profit; financial statements are attached
Tax on adjusted profit Based on the year's results 18% personal income tax + 5% military levy, unless exempt
Tax on dividends from the OÜ On receipt 9% personal income tax + 5% military levy
A controller is a Ukrainian resident with a stake of more than 50%, or more than 10% if Ukrainian residents together hold 50% or more, or with actual control. Since 2024, Ukraine has been receiving data on foreign accounts under the CRS standard.

Banks and payment services

For owners resident in Ukraine, banks and payment institutions carry out enhanced due diligence: source of funds, clients, sanctions risks. Contracts, invoices, a clear description of the model and a website help. More in our article how to open a bank account for an Estonian company.

Place of management

If all decisions are made in Ukraine, the Ukrainian side may see a permanent establishment in the company's activities. Contracts, board resolutions and the real role of the Estonian infrastructure must reflect the picture honestly: this is part of the set-up, not a formality.
fields.content_blocks_12_faq_items_0_question: Can a Ukrainian citizen open a company in Estonia?
fields.content_blocks_12_faq_items_0_answer: Yes. Through e-Residency, fully online; through a notary with a power of attorney; or with an Estonian ID card if you live in Estonia.
fields.content_blocks_12_faq_items_1_question: Where can I collect an e-resident card without leaving Ukraine?
fields.content_blocks_12_faq_items_1_answer: At the Estonian Embassy in Kyiv or at the mobile pick-up point in Lviv.
fields.content_blocks_12_faq_items_2_question: Do I need to file a CFC report in Ukraine?
fields.content_blocks_12_faq_items_2_answer: Yes, if you are a Ukrainian tax resident and control the company. The notice is due within 60 days of setting up the company and the report every year, even with zero profit.
fields.content_blocks_12_faq_items_3_question: Do I pay tax in Ukraine on the Estonian company's profit?
fields.content_blocks_12_faq_items_3_answer: If the total income of all your CFCs does not exceed €2 million a year, CFC profit is exempt from tax, but the report must still be filed. Dividends received personally are taxed at 9% personal income tax plus 5% military levy.
fields.content_blocks_12_faq_items_4_question: Can I pay my team in Ukraine through FOPs?
fields.content_blocks_12_faq_items_4_answer: Yes, but services from a supplier outside the EU are subject to Estonian VAT under the reverse charge. Without a standard VAT registration, the company pays 24% on these services with no deduction.
fields.content_blocks_12_faq_items_5_question: Can I close my FOP after opening an OÜ?
fields.content_blocks_12_faq_items_5_answer: You can, but you do not have to. Many keep their FOP for Ukrainian clients and use the OÜ for European ones.
fields.content_blocks_12_faq_items_6_question: Will a bank open an account for a company with a Ukrainian owner?
fields.content_blocks_12_faq_items_6_answer: The decision always lies with the bank, and the checks are enhanced. The chances are higher with contracts, a clear model and a website; many companies work through payment institutions.
fields.content_blocks_12_faq_items_7_question: What if I live in Estonia under temporary protection?
fields.content_blocks_12_faq_items_7_answer: You will not be issued e-Residency: the company is set up with an Estonian ID card. Check your tax residency, because it determines whether Ukrainian CFC rules apply.
